title: Perceptor: SLO-aware cost & latency attribution engine (per-route/model/customer)
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Objective: build ‘Perceptor’ — a near-real-time attribution engine that computes precise cost and latency breakdowns per route, model, and customer. This service must be SLO-aware (honor latency SLO buckets), reconcile streaming and batch-request footprints, and produce outputs consumable by the Console, billing rollups, and alerting pipelines.

Scope and constraints:
- Input signals: request traces (ingested from tracing pipeline), tokenized usage events, model configuration (quantization/profile info), routing decisions (fallbacks/variants), and autoscaler metadata (burst/reserved usage).
- Outputs: per-minute and hourly rollups for (route, model, customer) keys containing token_count, model_time_ms, queuing_ms, kernel_wait_ms, effective_cost_usd, batching_efficiency_score, and attribution_confidence.
- Latency SLO bucketing: attribute latency to categorized buckets (p50/p95/p99) and mark traces that forced SLO-tail fallbacks.
- Accuracy targets: per-customer cost error <= 1.5% for monthly totals, per-route latency bucket accuracy within 3% vs raw traces.
- RTO / freshness: near-real-time path with 90th percentile latency < 45s for the per-minute rollups; offline backfill runs support full reconstitution for any historical 30-day window within 6 hours.
acceptance_criteria: Service exposes a versioned API that returns per-(route,model,customer) rollups for requested time windows
Per-minute rollups available within 45s of event ingestion 90% of the time under normal load
Monthly cost totals per customer deviate < 1.5% from ground truth billing pipeline in a production-like test
Integration with Console cost dashboards (schema contract) and alerting hooks verified in staging
Backfill job can recompute any 30-day range within 6 hours and produce idempotent outputs
engineering_notes:
Design decisions: use a two-path pipeline — streaming fast-path (Kafka -> stateful aggregator -> materialized store) for per-minute rollups, and a batch reconciler (Spark/Beam) for hourly/daily aggregates and backfills. Attribution model will prefer token-level assignment when request-level token deltas are available; otherwise fall back to proportional attribution using model_time and redis-backed fingerprints. We'll encode SLO buckets as histogram aggregations and maintain per-customer correction factors to handle KV-cache hit skew. Store canonical outputs in the existing time-series store (TSDB) with a companion compact Parquet artifact for downstream billing. Implement strict idempotency using (ingest_epoch, event_fingerprint) keys.

Performance / cost trade-offs: the initial implementation will prioritize accuracy over absolute compute cost for the batch pipeline; streaming path will include heuristics to cap state size (eviction TTL per tenant) and emit sampled traces for heavy tenants to bound memory. Consider later adding quota-driven sampling tied to Dedicated customers to reduce tail compute.

Schema notes: the rollup row will be flat and include fields for route_id, model_id, customer_id, window_start_iso, window_granularity, token_count, compute_ms, queue_ms, kernel_wait_ms, cost_usd, batch_factor (float), slo_bucket (string), attribution_confidence (float), source_version (string).
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (MVP): implement streaming aggregator for per-minute rollups, output to tsdb + small materialized API. Phase 2: batch reconciler and backfill orchestration; expose detailed breakdowns per-model. Phase 3: add SLO-aware fallback analytics (flagging when variants caused changed costs) and tenant-level correction calibration. Phase 4: perf optimizations (incremental aggregation, quantization-aware cost modeling).
rollout_plan: 1) Deploy streaming aggregator to staging with 10% sampled traffic; 2) Run parallel validation against billing-sim in staging for 2 weeks; 3) Canary to 5% of prod traffic with read-only Console wiring; 4) Enable fully for non-critical tenants and monitor error budgets; 5) Full rollout with support on-call.
monitoring_and_metrics: track ingestion-lag_seconds P50/P95/P99, per_minute_rollups_emitted_rate, backfill_job_latency_seconds, per_customer_cost_error_pct (vs billing-sim), memory_per_tenant_mb, aggregator_backpressure_events. Create a Console dashboard tile for quick triage and a PagerDuty runbook.
tests_and_validation: unit tests for attribution math; integration tests with synthetic traces covering streaming + batch convergence; large-scale e2e validation using historical production trace dump; chaos tests to simulate drop-in/fallback routing. Golden dataset for monthly cost must be produced and checked into labels/fixtures for CI.
data_governance: Outputs labeled with source_version and computation_run_id. Respect PII rules: customer identifiers are hashed at rest in Parquet artifacts, and the Console will only display human-readable names after ACL checks. All artifacts land in the project-specific bucket with lifecycle rules.
security_considerations: No plaintext secrets in the pipeline. Service will run with least-privilege service account. If cross-tenant data joins are required for debugging, require approval and audit log entries. Security review flagged for phase 3 (tenant correction calibration) but initial run does not require additional review.
